title: ops: prereqs checklist (Google / OpenAI / Atlassian / Notion creds)
description:
Human action items the team owns. Blocks running the stack end-to-end; does not block code if mocks are used.

Google Workspace:
- Cloud project; enable Calendar API, Meet REST API, Drive API
- OAuth Client (Web): GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID + GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET; authorized redirect http://localhost:8000/auth/google/callback
- Service Account: JSON key -> data/keys/sa_key.json
- Workspace Admin: domain-wide delegation for SA client_id with scopes:
  - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly
  - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.readonly
  - https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly
- GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_SUBJECT (admin email for impersonation)
- Workspace plan with native Meet transcripts (Business Standard+)

OpenAI:
- OPENAI_API_KEY (model gpt-4.1-mini default)

Atlassian:
- API token at atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens -> ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN
- ATLASSIAN_MCP_URL default https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/sse

Notion:
- Integration token at notion.so/my-integrations -> NOTION_TOKEN
- Share target parent page with the integration
- NOTION_MCP_URL default https://mcp.notion.com/v1/sse

Test data:
- 1 @municorn.com test user
- 1 calendar with 2+ ended Meet events that have transcripts
- 1 sandbox Jira project + 1 sandbox Notion parent page

Deliverable: filled .env at repo root + data/keys/sa_key.json on disk.
acceptance_criteria: .env populated; sa_key.json mounted; sanity script in backend hits each provider successfully

title: backend: Runtime Orchestrator (DeepAgents)
description:
DeepAgents-based runtime; owns agent lifecycle and the only place handoffs happen. Enforces capability boundaries.

Scope:
- app/runtime/contracts.py: RunMode, AgentName enum, RunContext, HandoffTarget, TraceEvent, ProposedUpdate
- app/runtime/orchestrator.py:
  - start_run(entry_agent, ctx) -> run_id
  - dispatch_handoff(from_agent, to_agent, payload) — mediated, recorded
  - shared services (llm, rag, trace) gated by per-agent allow-list
  - Agents cannot call each other directly
- Records every step in trace_store

Boundary matrix per wiki/domains/agents.md.

Reference: wiki/modules/runtime-orchestrator.md.
acceptance_criteria: tests verify allow-list (e.g. user_chat cannot call mcp); handoffs recorded in trace; agent-to-agent direct calls rejected

title: backend: LLM Gateway (langchain-openai wrapper)
description:
Single chokepoint for all OpenAI calls. Per wiki/decisions: OpenAI only.

Scope:
- app/llm.py with thin wrapper around ChatOpenAI
- Env: OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL (default gpt-4.1-mini)
- Streaming support (used by SSE chat)
- Per-call temperature/system override
- Caller-tagged usage logging (model, tokens, latency) -> trace
- TDD: mock OpenAI client; verify retry on transient errors

Reference: wiki/modules/llm-gateway.md.
acceptance_criteria: unit tests pass with mocked OpenAI; streaming yields chunks; misconfig raises at startup

title: backend: Google OAuth login + JWT (@municorn.com only)
description:
Login flow + session. Required by every authenticated endpoint.

Scope:
- /auth/google/start -> redirect to Google consent
- /auth/google/callback -> exchange code, verify hd claim == ALLOWED_DOMAIN, upsert user, issue JWT
- JWT verification dep used by all protected routers
- 403 for non-@municorn.com users
- Refresh handling decided per JWT TTL (24h default)

Env: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, ALLOWED_DOMAIN, SECRET_KEY.
Frontend already has /login page; this provides the real backend.

Reference: wiki/flows/oauth-login.md, wiki/domains/deployment.md (security posture).
acceptance_criteria: tests cover happy path, non-allowed-domain rejection, expired/invalid JWT rejection

title: backend: SQLAlchemy models + schema
description:
Persistence layer. Defines all tables needed by routers and agents.

Tables (per wiki/domains/backend.md):
- users (id, email, name, allowed_domain check, created_at)
- meetings (id, google_event_id, title, start, end, organizer, attendees, has_meet)
- meeting_artifacts (id, meeting_id, type=transcript|notes|recording, source, content_ref, fetched_at)
- updates (id, target=jira|notion, action, payload_json, status=staged|approved|rejected|applied, source_run_id)
- trace_runs (id, entry_agent, started_at, finished_at, status)
- trace_steps (id, run_id, agent, kind=llm|tool|handoff, input_json, output_json, ts)
- integrations (key, value_encrypted_or_ref) — for settings UI

Schema bootstrap via Base.metadata.create_all on startup (no Alembic for MVP). Pydantic schemas in app/schemas/. TDD: write model tests first.
acceptance_criteria: pytest covers create/read for each table; FK integrity enforced; secrets never stored plaintext

title: backend: routers chat + meetings + updates + settings + trace
description:
HTTP surface exposed to the frontend. JWT-protected. Each wires the corresponding agent or store.

Routers (per wiki/domains/backend.md):
- POST /chat (SSE stream) -> user_chat
- GET /meetings, /meetings/{id}, /meetings/{id}/transcript, /meetings/{id}/summary, /meetings/{id}/actions, /meetings/{id}/decisions, /meetings/{id}/outputs
- GET /updates, POST /updates/{id}/approve|reject|apply -> jira_notion
- GET/PUT /settings (secrets never returned in clear)
- GET /trace, GET /trace/{run_id}, GET /trace/{run_id}/steps

TDD: contract tests per router using TestClient. Auth dep required on every protected route.
acceptance_criteria: contract tests cover happy + auth-failure paths; SSE streams chunks; settings PUT roundtrip never leaks secrets

title: backend: agent jira_notion (staged writes + HITL)
description:
Owns every Jira/Notion read and write. One of three fixed agents. Sole writer of staged updates.

Scope:
- backend/app/agents/jira_notion.py
- Reads via MCP clients (safe tools only without staging)
- Risky writes (issue update, page edit) -> persisted to updates table as status=staged
- Auto-create/append meeting notes in permitted Notion parent (no staging required per wiki/domains/integrations.md)
- apply_staged(update_id) called by /updates/approve router
- Cannot read Google artifacts; cannot compose chat final answer

Reference: wiki/concepts/human-in-the-loop.md.
acceptance_criteria: staged update lifecycle covered (stage->approve->apply / stage->reject); auto-append distinguished from risky write; refuses Google reads

title: backend: agent user_chat
description:
Owns the user-facing chat answer. One of three fixed agents.

Scope:
- backend/app/agents/user_chat.py
- Inputs: user message, conversation history
- Pipeline:
  1. RAG retrieve relevant chunks
  2. Decide if live Jira/Notion needed -> request handoff to jira_notion
  3. Compose streaming answer with inline citations
- Cannot make external writes; cannot bypass orchestrator

TDD: mocked rag + llm; verify citation pass-through and handoff trigger.
acceptance_criteria: streamed answer carries citations; live-context handoff covered; refuses external writes

title: backend: agent meeting_participation
description:
Owns Google Calendar/Meet ingest and meeting analysis. One of three fixed agents.

Scope:
- backend/app/agents/meeting_participation.py
- Trigger: scheduled sync OR explicit re-sync request
- Pipeline (see wiki/flows/meeting-processing.md):
  1. calendar_sync.list_events + fetch_meet_artifacts
  2. Normalize into SQLite
  3. LLM analysis via llm gateway: summary, action_items, decisions, blockers
  4. Index transcript + summary into RAG
  5. If references found -> hand off to jira_notion via orchestrator
- Cannot touch MCP directly

TDD with mocked calendar_sync, llm, rag.
acceptance_criteria: full pipeline test (mocked deps); refuses to call MCP directly; trace recorded
